items.title: Wayne Bergeron interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 29, 2020
items.q: I just heard Wynton Marsalis clam a note right now, and he doesn’t make mistakes.

ctx.x: Especially if it’s the trumpet, because hear that right now? I just heard Wynton Marsalis clam a note right now, and he doesn’t make mistakes. So of course, and usually it’s kind of funny, especially if it’s a big clam you know, and you’ve played it right five times in a row you know, and then it might make people laugh. Like, “Oh that’s the keeper, all right, great.” So of course the goal is not to make any mistakes, but I come from the mindset of, I try not to play too carefully. I try to play as musically as…
I’m glad you mentioned Bobby Shew because he told me a little thing that he learned from someone else, that helped him keep sane in the studio and that was, “You play this and I’ll play that.”
